column2: The Grand Theogonist Cast Out

Word has come that [grand_theogonist.GetTitledName] has lost the last of the temple's lands to the swords of [grand_theogonist.GetHerHis] enemies. The Grand Theogonist still holds the high seat of the cult of Sigmar, but not a single field or keep in [grand_theogonist.GetHerHis] own name.\n\nIn every temple of the Heldenhammer the priests are praying for the day the cult's lands are won back, and asking aloud which of the faithful will win them.

The last of the temple's lands are lost. I still hold the high seat of the cult of Sigmar, and the faithful still kneel when I pass, but I no longer hold a single field or keep in my own name. Every heretic and rival in the Empire will hear of it and laugh.\n\nThe priests pray for a champion who will win the cult's lands back. So do I.
Sigmar will raise up a champion.
This shame will be answered, in Sigmar's name!
Grim news for the faithful.
The Most Serene Republic of [From.GetBaseName]

For generations the merchant houses of [Root.Capital.GetName] have grown rich on every cargo that passed our quays. Our ships carry wine, silk and powder from Tilea to Marienburg and beyond, our banks lend gold to princes, and our mercenaries fight the wars of lords who sneer at us as shopkeepers.\n\nNo longer. Today the Council has proclaimed the Most Serene Republic of [From.GetBaseName], a crown held not by blood but by coin. Let the old nobility count its quarterings. We will count their debts.
Gold rules the world, and we rule the gold.
Together we will hold these lands.
We shall see how long it lasts.
Refound the Eagle Confederacy
The princes of the eastern Border Princes once swore to stand together beneath the eagle banner against the orcs of the Badlands. Raise that banner again.
Refound the Northern Border Confederacy
The northern princes, caught between the Black Mountains and the greenskin tribes, once made a league of mutual defence. Call them together again.
Refound the Principality of Khypria
Khypria lies empty of a prince. Hold its seat at Khypris and enough land around it, and you may take the old crown for yourself.
Refound the Principality of Myrmidens
Myrmidens, the city of the warrior goddess, has no prince. Hold its seat and enough land around it, and you may restore the principality in Myrmidia's name.
The Eagle Confederacy
The Northern Border Confederacy
The Principality of Khypria
The Principality of Myrmidens

In the Border Princes every prince stands alone, and every prince who stands alone is sooner or later overrun by the orcs coming down out of the Badlands. At Galiti I have called the princes together under the old eagle banner, and they have sworn to answer each other's call to war.\n\nThey have chosen me as the first among them. None of us will stand alone again, or so we swear today.

The princes of the north know better than most what lies in the Black Mountains and what comes out of them each spring. At Brovska I have called them together, and they have sworn to defend each other's walls as if they were their own.\n\nThe Northern Border Confederacy is reborn, and I am its first prince.

Khypria has gone too long without a prince. Every adventurer and sellsword in the Border Princes has fought over its fields, and none has held them for long. Now its seat at Khypris and the lands around it are mine, and I have taken up the old crown of the principality.\n\nLet the other princes take note. Khypria has a master again.

Myrmidens was founded by followers of Myrmidia, and the goddess of war has watched over it since. Now it has a prince again. I hold its seat and the lands about it, and I have taken up the crown of the principality.\n\nMay the Shield of Myrmidia guard it better than its last prince did.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has called the princes of the east together at Galiti and refounded the Eagle Confederacy. The members have sworn to answer each other's call to war against the orcs. In the Border Princes, oaths like these rarely outlast their princes. But while they hold, the Confederacy is a power to reckon with.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has called the northern princes together at Brovska, and they have refounded the Northern Border Confederacy as a league of mutual defence. The greenskins of the Black Mountains will find the passes harder to force. Some of the princes may find their neighbours harder to rob, too.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] now holds Khypris and the lands about it, and has taken up the old crown of the Principality of Khypria. Another prince has risen in the Border Princes. The question, as ever, is how long [From.GetSheHe] will keep the crown.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] now holds Myrmidens and the lands about it, and has taken up the crown of the principality in Myrmidia's name. Another prince has risen in the Border Princes. The question, as ever, is how long [From.GetSheHe] will keep the crown.
Proclaim the East March

Ostermark is the Empire's eastern shield, facing the haunted hills of Sylvania, the troubled steppe of Kislev and the mountains where the greenskins breed. Proclaim it the East March, and make its Elector the Warden of the eastern frontier.
Your liege approves (opinion of at least 25)
Petition to be Grand Prince of Ostland
The Electors of Ostland have long called themselves Grand Princes. Ostland has no prince now. With the Emperor's favour, you may take the crown of the Grand Principality as a vassal of the Emperor.
You are of the Emperor's dynasty
The Emperor favours you (opinion of at least 50)
Raise the Knights of the Griffon Again
The Knights of the Griffon, the Templars who guard the Temple of Sigmar, have fallen. Call on the faithful to raise the order again.
The §YKnights of the Griffon§! are raised again, with a new Grand Master sworn to you.
Warden of the East March
This ruler holds Ostermark as the East March, the Empire's shield against Sylvania, Kislev's troubles and the greenskins of the mountains.
The East March

Ostermark has always been the Empire's eastern shield. To the south lie the haunted hills of Sylvania, to the east the steppe of Kislev and the mountains where the greenskins breed, and every war of the east is fought first on our fields.\n\nToday I have proclaimed Ostermark the East March. Its keeps will be manned, its levies drilled, and its Elector will stand as Warden of the eastern frontier. Let the dead and the orcs come. The March is ready.
The East March stands.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has proclaimed Ostermark the East March and named [From.GetHerselfHimself] Warden of the eastern frontier. The keeps along the borders of Sylvania and Kislev are being manned and the levies drilled. Some at court mutter that a Warden with an army so ready could turn it on [From.GetHerHis] neighbours as easily as on the dead.
Better Ostermark's swords than ours.
The Grand Prince of Ostland

The Electors of Ostland have always called themselves Grand Princes, whatever the rest of the Empire called them. Now the Emperor has granted it in truth. I hold the crown of the Grand Principality of Ostland, a vassal of the Emperor still, but a prince among counts.\n\nThe lords of the Forest of Shadows will learn to bow lower than they used to.
Long live the Emperor, and Ostland!

By the Emperor's favour, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been raised to Grand Prince of Ostland. The old Electors of Ostland always claimed the style. Now one has it with an Imperial seal, and the other Electors wonder who will be favoured next.
A prince among counts, is it?
The Fall of Araby

For centuries the Sultans of Araby raided the coasts of the Old World and sent their armies into Estalia. The knights of the Errantry Wars won battles in the deserts, but never the land.\n\nNow Araby is mine. From Al-Haikk to the edge of the Great Desert, the crown of the Sultans has passed to a ruler of the Old World. The bards will sing of this for a thousand years, and my blood will carry the tale.
Let the deserts remember my name.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has taken the crown of Araby. The lands of the Sultans, from Al-Haikk to the edge of the Great Desert, are ruled from the Old World for the first time. The knights who fought in the Errantry Wars dreamed of this. Few believed it would happen.

The unbeliever [From.GetTitledFirstName] has seized the crown of Araby. The lands of the Sultans are ruled by a lord of the Old World, and the faithful of the Great Lord weep in the temples of Al-Haikk. But the desert has swallowed greater armies than this one.
Who would have believed it?
The desert will take it back.
The Griffons Return

The Knights of the Griffon guarded the Temple of Sigmar from the days of Magnus the Pious, until their order fell. Today the call has gone out through every temple of the Heldenhammer, and the faithful have answered. A new Grand Master has taken the vows, and the griffon banner flies again over the Temple.
Sigmar's temple has its guardians again.
Blood of the Conqueror of Araby
[This.GetSheHeCap] is a legend in the Old World for taking the crown of Araby and ruling the lands of the Sultans.
Union of the Old Peoples
Old Peoples'
Great Khan
Great Khan-Queen
Unite the Old Peoples

Long before Khan-Queen Miska rode out of the east, the Ungols ran their horses on the oblast and the Ropsmenn kept their stanitsas by the rivers. The Gospodars took the land and now want the blood too, calling every child of the steppe a Kislevite. If both peoples ride under one banner, no tsar will ever make Gospodars of them.
Your realm holds at least 8 provinces of Ungol culture
Your realm holds at least 5 provinces of Ropsmann culture
The Ungol and Ropsmann lands and lords of the union will not take up the Kislevite culture while the union stands.
The Union of the Old Peoples

The khans came to the old kurgans on the steppe, Ungol and Ropsmann both, and a hag of the Ungols cut a mare's throat before them. Each khan dipped a hand in the blood and pressed it to the same white felt, and the felt was raised on spears so the wind could see it.\n\nThe Gospodars came to this land with Miska and call it theirs. Let them. The old peoples remember who rode here first, and from this day they ride together, under [Root.GetFirstName], Great Khan of the Union of the Old Peoples.

The stanitsa elders came up the rivers and the Ungol khans rode in from the steppe, and they met at the old kurgans as their grandfathers' grandfathers did before the Gospodars came. They drank kvas from one horn, spat on the ground towards Kislev city, and swore that no child of theirs would ever be made a Gospodar.\n\nThe tsars have their crown of ice. The old peoples have [Root.GetFirstName], Great Khan of the Union of the Old Peoples, and every bow and blade the oblast can raise.
Call the riders. Let the tsar count our horses.
The kurgans have heard us. That is enough for now.

Word comes from the oblast that [From.GetTitledName] has gathered the Ungol and Ropsmann khans at the old kurgans and had [From.GetHerselfHimself] raised on white felt as Great Khan of a Union of the Old Peoples. The boyars are furious. The Ice Witches say nothing, which is worse.\n\nThey will not kneel as Kislevites, these people. They say their blood was here before Miska's, and they mean to keep it.

The riders came through at a gallop with the news. [From.GetTitledName] has united the Ungols and Ropsmenn as the Union of the Old Peoples, and the old blood will not be made Gospodar. In every stanitsa they are lighting fires and singing the songs the tsar's priests forbade.

Word comes from the oblast that [From.GetTitledName] has united the Ungol and Ropsmann khans as the Union of the Old Peoples. The old peoples of Kislev mean to stay as they are, whatever the tsar says. There will be blood over this, sooner or later.
Traitors to Ursun and to the throne. I will remember this.
The old blood rides again!
Kislev was never one people anyway.
I am pleased to hear that after a period of peace and shrewd management the county of [From.GetName] is doing very well. People are happy and the tax collectors are reporting record intakes.
[From.GetName] prospers!

As the prosperity of [Root.GetName] increases, land which was previously considered marginal is increasing in value. With the proper incentives, it should be possible to clear enough land to found a new holding upon.
I know a good deal when I see one!
It's too expensive
The workshops of [Root.GetName] have a need for large numbers of new workers. By offering a bonus, it would be possible to make sure these workers are [Root.Holder.Culture.GetName].
Make it so
Leave it to chance

As commerce in [Root.GetName] grows, a number of Strigany caravans have requested permission to settle their families in one of the towns so they can manage their business more effectively. This would likely lead to increased tax revenues, but local religious authorities will disapprove.
Invite them in!
Begone!
People are flocking to [Root.GetName], and they should know your name! By constructing a great monument there, you can be assured that everyone will know who to credit.
I am great!
Don't make a fuss
Some buffoon has built a big statue of themselves here. Tearing it down and selling the gold-plating should fetch a few coins.
Due to the great number of merchant ships docking in the ports of [Root.GetName], there is increased demand for expanded harbor space. Of course, larger harbors could also service more warships...
Indeed they could!
[Root.Owner.PrimaryTitle.GetName] is a land power!
The prosperity of [Root.GetName] has attracted a number of scholars who are now looking for a patron. Organizing them into a foundation for learning could result in useful new discoveries.
Knowledge is power!
Money is power!
The prosperity of [Root.GetName] has prompted an increasing desire for a Great Library in the country so that learned people there can always find entertainment.
As people flock to [Root.GetName], so too do the clergy. In fact, so many have arrived that with a donation to get them started, [Root.GetName] could become a notable center of worship.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodNameCap] wills it!
Will [Root.Religion.GetHighGodNameCap] pay for it?

The prime quality wood found in the forests of [Root.GetName] has attracted the attention of a group of elite artisans. These renowned individuals have set up a concern where they offer their services for a hefty price. For the right price you could acquire their services and put them to work for the crown!
They should work towards the betterment of the realm!
I will banish them and seize their assets.

For quite some time now, more and more miners have started mining for ore and breaking stone in the mountains of [Root.GetName]. It has come to the point where there is a massive network of them, all organized into various interconnected guilds. For a hefty sum you could bring these guilds into the employ of the crown!
They shall serve me and the people of [Root.GetName]!
They are clearly trespassing, get rid of them and seize their tools!

A large number of people from a religious minority has petitioned you for permission to settle in [Root.GetName]. This would likely lead to increased tax revenues, but local religious authorities will disapprove.
Invite them in!
Begone!

For some time now, the county of [Root.GetName] has served as an unofficial training ground for your armies as there is plenty of open space on which to train and abundant food to feed the troops. A group of senior officers are now petitioning you for money in order to erect an official regimental camp in the county!
That sounds like an excellent suggestion!
Having it easy would just make them weaker.
I will let [councillor_target.GetFirstName] oversee the construction!
Sadly, I cannot afford this.

Lots of peasants have been moving to the county of [prosperity_target.GetName] lately. Your [Root.GetTreasurerName], [councillor_target.GetFullName], suggests building new roads in order to make it easier for the peasants to reach the central holdings. [councillor_target.GetSheHeCap] insists that in doing so the county would become more prosperous!
Less traveling means more work being done!
A waste of money.

The peasants in [prosperity_target.GetName] spend a long time on the road in order to meet with the [prosperity_target.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s, or so your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [councillor_target.GetFirstName] claims. [councillor_target.GetSheHeCap] suggests that it would be in your interests to construct local shrines, in that way the peasants would not have to travel far in order to worship.
A safe peasant is a productive peasant.
Unfortunately, I have no money to spare.

According to your [Root.GetMarshalName], [councillor_target.GetFullName], the peasants of [prosperity_target.GetName] are having frequent troubles with highwaymen and wild beasts. [councillor_target.GetSheHeCap] suggests constructing a series of outposts along the roads of [prosperity_target.GetName]. The peasantry would feel much safer, and it might even lead to more peasants moving to the county!
Ah yes, an excellent idea!
My money is better spent elsewhere.

The peasants of [prosperity_target.GetName] are quite far apart and spread out. Your [Root.GetSpymasterName], [councillor_target.GetFullName], suggests investing in a provincial messenger system so that they can communicate with their kin more easily. [councillor_target.GetSheHeCap] claims that doing so would attract more peasants to the county!
A peculiar tradition, I will support it!
I will not waste my money on such nonsense.

According to [Root.GetChancellorName] [councillor_target.GetFirstName], the peasants of [prosperity_target.GetName] have started a delightful tradition where the peasantry from several villages meet up and dance, feast and pair up for future marriage. By promoting this tradition [councillor_target.GetFirstName] believes that the county will develop a strong local culture that will attract more peasants!
It is time for me to visit [prosperity_target.GetName]!
I do not have time for this.

Being such an industrious ruler you have not gone unnoticed by the population of [prosperity_target.GetName]. By paying the county elders a personal visit, they would surely be inspired and the peasants would feel particularly appreciated. A small donation would also go a long way, of course.
Ask for Money
[FromFrom.GetSubjectPronounCap] will owe me a Favor...
Anything for my liege!
Respectfully refuse
Traitorously Refuse

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

While I understand your reasons and respect your ambition, I need you to end your destructive war against [target_defender.GetTitledName]. I am sure we could come to some arrangement.

With respect, [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

While my grievance with [target_defender.GetTitledName] will remain, I would not dream of refusing such a reasonable request by my liege!

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
My liege is gracious!

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I have arranged for [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] to end [FromFrom.GetPossPronoun] unjust war against you with a White Peace.

With respect, [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
Very well, this war must end!
I cannot afford that...

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am willing to end my war against [target_defender.GetTitledName] in return for a modest sum of money. This affair has been costly, and a white peace means a loss of face.

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am willing to compensate you for your lost prestige in your acceptance of a white peace with [target_defender.GetTitledName]. I am pleased the affair is ended.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
I will win anyway!

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Although I understand you want compensation for your acceptance of a white peace in your war against with [target_defender.GetTitledName], I cannot afford the sum you requested. Good luck on the battlefield!

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
Most unfortunate...
The law says this is treason!

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

While it grieves me deeply, I simply cannot end my war with [target_defender.GetTitledName] at this time. The die has been cast.

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
No, I will not be in debt to [From.GetObjectPronoun]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am willing to end my war against [target_defender.GetTitledName]. However, the affair has been costly and I would lose face, so you would owe me a comparable Favor...

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I realize you will lose prestige in your acceptance of a white peace with [target_defender.GetTitledName]. I am in your debt, and promise to assist you when you ask for a favor.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Although I understand you seek compensation for your acceptance of a white peace in your war against with [target_defender.GetTitledName], I will not be indebted to you. Good luck on the battlefield!

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
I cannot refuse

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am calling in that favor you owe me. I need you to stop your war against [target_defender.GetTitledName] immediately and accept a white peace...

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Of course I will end my war with [target_defender.GetTitledName], but I am no longer in your debt...

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
[FromFrom.GetSubjectPronounCap] will owe me a big Favor for this!

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

You must surrender to [target_attacker.GetTitledName]. [target_attacker.GetPossPronounCap] cause is just. However, I am a reasonable [FromFrom.GetManWoman] and I am sure we could come to some arrangement.

With respect, [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I stand to lose much in [target_attacker.GetTitledName]'s war of aggression, but I would never dream of refusing you, my liege!

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I have arranged for [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] to surrender to you and accept the outcome. One day, I might call on you to repay this favor...

With respect, [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Though I stand to lose much, I am willing to surrender to [target_attacker.GetTitledName] in return for a large sum of money. I am sure you understand.

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am willing to compensate you for your lost prestige in your acceptance of a white peace with [target_defender.GetTitledName]. I am pleased the affair is ended.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
I shall win this war!

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Your wish for monetary compensation is understandable. One does not surrender easily. However, I cannot afford the sum you requested. Good luck on the battlefield!

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I wish I could comply with your desire, but I cannot simply surrender to the dastardly [target_attacker.GetTitledName]. I stand to lose too much!

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am willing to surrender to [target_attacker.GetTitledName]. However, the loss would be devastating, so you would owe me a comparable Favor...

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I know full well what you stand to lose by surrendering to [target_attacker.GetTitledName]. I am in your debt, and promise to assist you when you ask for a favor in return!

Most gratefully, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I understand your reluctance to surrender in this war with [target_attacker.GetTitledName], which to you must seem deeply unjust. However, I will not be indebted to you. Good luck on the battlefield!

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am calling in that favor you owe me. Though I realize what it will cost you, I need you to surrender to [target_attacker.GetTitledName]. Trust me, it is for the best...

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Surrendering to the loathsome [target_attacker.GetTitledName] makes me ill, but I am an honorable [From.GetManWoman] and acknowledge the favor I owe you. The debt has now been repaid.

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
[FromFrom.GetSubjectPronounCap] will owe me a big Favor for this!

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

For the long-term good of the realm, I must ask you to change succession law to Gavelkind.

With respect, [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am not keen on Gavelkind Law, but I would never dream of refusing you, my liege!

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
Very well...

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am not thrilled at instituting Gavelkind law, but I will comply in return for a large sum of money. I am sure you understand.

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am willing to compensate you fairly in return for your institution of Gavelkind law. Your wisdom serves your people well.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
My realm shall not be divided!

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Your wish for monetary compensation in return for Gavelkind law is understandable. However, I cannot afford the sum you requested.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I wish I could comply with your desire, but Gavelkind law will not serve my descendants well. I am afraid I must refuse.

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am willing to institute Gavelkind law. However, it would clearly not be in my best interests, so you would owe me a comparable Favor...

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Thank you for instituting Gavelkind law. I am in your debt, and promise to assist you when you ask for a favor in return!

Most gratefully, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I do understand your reluctance to change to Gavelkind succession. However, I will not be indebted to you. With some disappointment.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To my loyal vassal, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

I am calling in that favor you owe me. I need you to change succession law to Gavelkind. Trust me, it is for the best...

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

To the [GetFromRootCompliment], [Root.GetTitledFirstName].

Gavelkind is a divisive law that will cause problems for my descendants, but I am an honorable [From.GetManWoman] and acknowledge the favor I owe you. The debt has now been repaid.

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
[Root.GetName] Prospers!
Become the Saoshyant

The prophets of Ormazd foretold a saviour who would unite the lands of Araby under the Holy Flame and drive the servants of Ahgriman back into the dark. All of Araby is mine, and the faithful look to me. Let them hail me as the Saoshyant.
Forge the §Y[Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] Crown§! for the treasury of [Root.GetTitledFirstName]
Crown of the Saoshyant
[saoshyant_creator.GetOnlyDynastyName] Crown
A crown of red gold and sunstone forged for the Saoshyant of Ormazd, the saviour the prophets promised, who united all Araby under the Holy Flame.
The promised Saoshyant, saviour of the world and holy icon of the faith of Ormazd, who united Araby under the Holy Flame.
The Saoshyant

From Copher to the Great Desert the fire-temples blaze through the night. The scholars of Ormazd have searched the Prophets and found what the faithful already knew: I am the Saoshyant, the promised saviour, born to unite Araby under the Holy Flame and to break the servants of Ahgriman. In their temples the followers of the false prophets tremble.
The Holy Flame burns in me.

News from Araby: [From.GetTitledName] holds all the lands of the desert for the faith of Ormazd, and the fire-priests hail [From.GetHerHim] as the Saoshyant, the saviour promised by their Prophets. The rival faiths of Araby are in disarray.
Praise Ormazd! The promised one has come!
A false saviour, and our faith is shaken.
The desert folk have a new prophet. How quaint.
Landfall in the New World

Months after they left harbour, my ships have reached the steaming coast of Lustria, the land of gold and serpents that every sailor tells stories about and none believes. Now [landfall_county.GetName] flies my banner, the first land in Lustria held by men of our kind. The jungle hums with insects and stranger things, the ruins are crusted with gold, and the scouts swear they have seen cold-blooded warriors watching from the trees. Whatever waits in there, the New World has been opened, and the name of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] will always be the first in its story.

My ships have made landfall on the cold black shores of Naggaroth, the Land of Chill, where the Dark Elves raise their towers. Now [landfall_county.GetName] flies my banner, the first land in Naggaroth held by men. The winds smell of iron and the forests of old blood, and every night the sentries hear the slave-drums of the Druchii. It is a bitter prize, but it is mine.

The skalds have sung of it since the days of Losteriksson: Skeggi, the great hall that the Norse raised on the coast of Lustria, far across the western sea. Now the sons of Norsca hold [landfall_county.GetName] again. The longships lie drawn up on a beach of black sand, the jungle steams behind the palisade, and gold from the old temples is already being weighed in the hall. The Gods will be watching.
Let the whole world hear of it.

Sailors in every port speak of nothing else: [From.GetTitledName] has taken land on the coast of Lustria, the first of our kind to rule a piece of the New World. Already the adventurers and treasure-hunters are crowding the docks, desperate for a place on the next ship west.

Word has come from the far west: [From.GetTitledName] has planted a banner on the black shores of Naggaroth, in the very land of the Dark Elves. Some call it madness, others call it the boldest deed of the age.

The longships are back: [From.GetTitledName] holds Skeggi on the coast of Lustria, the old Norse colony of Losteriksson. Every coastal town between Marienburg and Erengrad is wondering how long it will be before Lustrian gold pays for Norscan raids.
The New World is calling.
The Merchant from Cathay

The whole Old World is talking about a merchant of Miragliano who set out along the Ivory Road twenty years ago and was long given up for dead. Now he has come home in a coat of dragon-embroidered silk, with chests of jade and porcelain and a book of marvels. He tells of the Great Bastion that guards Cathay against the Chaos hordes, of cities greater than Altdorf and Nuln together, and of the Dragon Emperor who has ruled for a thousand years. The scholars call him a liar. The merchant guilds are already fitting out caravans.
Cathay! Could it all be true?
The Treasure Fleet

At dawn the lookouts of the harbour cried out in fear: a fleet of junks larger than any ship ever seen in Araby had appeared on the horizon, red sails filling the sky. It is a treasure fleet of Cathay, sent by the Dragon Emperor to show his glory to the lands of the west. Its admiral has come ashore with gifts of silk, jade and caged beasts no one can name, and the sultans of Araby are vying with one another to receive him.
Truly the East is full of wonders.
The Red Cord on the Roads
Stranglers of the Red Cord, a murder-cult of Khaine, haunt the roads of this province. Merchants and pilgrims stay away.

Reports come from [murdercult_province.GetName]: travellers are vanishing on the roads. Merchants, pilgrims, even a party of armed guards, gone without a trace. The peasants whisper of the Red Cord, worshippers of Khaine, the Lord of Murder, who strangle the unwary with a crimson cord and cut out their hearts for their god.
Send agents to find out what is happening.
Robbers and wolves, nothing more.
The agents I sent to [murdercult_province.GetName] have vanished too. Last week a shepherd found one of them in a ditch, a red silk cord around his neck and a hole where his heart should be.
Keep searching. Find these murderers.
Hang a few villagers. The rest will talk.
Let the roads go. It is not worth the cost.

The villagers I hanged died swearing they knew nothing, and it seems they told the truth: the killings go on. Every week more travellers vanish on the roads of [murdercult_province.GetName], and now the peasants fear my soldiers as much as the stranglers.
Hire witch hunters. They know these cults.
I have done all I can.

The witch hunters have tracked the Red Cord to the woods and the hill shrines of [murdercult_province.GetName], but the cultists melt into the crowd by day: farmers, innkeepers, a priest. To root them out I will need soldiers on every road.
Send the soldiers, whatever it costs.
A few patrols will have to do.
The Red Cord

A new servant brought my wine tonight. As I reached for the cup a crimson cord flashed toward my throat, and [murdercult_guardian.GetTitledFirstName] threw [murdercult_guardian.GetHerselfHimself] between us. By the time the guards had cut the strangler down, my saviour lay dead on the floor, the red cord still drawn tight.
[murdercult_guardian.GetFirstName] died for me.

A new servant brought my wine tonight. As I reached for the cup a crimson cord flashed toward my throat. I fought for my life alone on the floor of my own hall until the guards burst in, and I will carry the marks of that cord for the rest of my days.
I am alive. Khaine will have to wait.
My council sits pale and silent around the table. The Red Cord has reached into my own hall. Some urge me to hunt the cult to the last man, others to stay behind my walls until the danger has passed.
Hunt them down. Every last one.
Double the guards. I am not leaving this room.

My riders have searched [murdercult_province.GetName] from end to end and found nothing but empty shrines and old bloodstains. The Red Cord is still out there. One last great sweep might finish them, but it will empty my treasury.
Pay it. End this.
Enough. Let the roads look after themselves.

The great sweep has done its work. No traveller has vanished in [murdercult_province.GetName] for months, and the last shrine of the Red Cord was found burned and empty. Wherever the stranglers have gone, they are no longer my problem.
Good riddance.

The war against [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] is won. The bells have not stopped ringing since the news came, and my captains are already asking when the army will march through the capital beneath its banners. The people want to see the standards of the beaten foe dragged in the dust, the priests want to bless the victors at the temple steps, and every lord of my realm wants to be seen riding at my side.\n\nA triumph would cost a great deal. Refusing one would cost more.

The hordes of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] have broken against my walls and fled back into the north. Where the Dark Gods' banners passed, villages burned and the dead hang from every tree, but the tide has turned. My people have stood against the end of the world and lived.\n\nThe temples ring their bells day and night. The common folk weep in the streets. They want to see the army that saved them, and they want to see the black standards burned in the square.

[triumph_foe.GetTitledName] lies broken and his lands are mine to despoil. The warriors of my horde howl around the fires and the shamans say the Dark Gods have watched the slaughter with pleasure.\n\nThe gods expect their tithe. The warriors expect to see their champion raised up on a mound of skulls before the whole host, and every chieftain who fought for me expects his share of the glory. A champion who skimps on the offering is soon a champion no longer.

The war against [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] is won, and the reckoning is entered in the Book of Grudges. The clans who marched with me have come home with their dead on their shields, and the halls are full of beards waiting to drink to the fallen.\n\nBy the old custom the victory must be honoured in the ancestor halls, with a great feast and the names of the dead carved in stone. The Elders are watching to see how open my hand will be.

Da war against [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] iz won and everyone knows it was me wot won it. Da boyz are already piling up da heads and da loot in da middle of camp and arguing about who gets da shiniest bits.\n\nDey want a big feast, a bigga heap of trophies and a proper shout of WAAAGH so loud da gods can hear it. If da boss don't give 'em one, some big lad might start finkin' he could do better.

[triumph_foe.GetTitledName] is beaten and his kin weep in chains in the holds of my ships. My corsairs and spearmen have returned with slaves and plunder, and the whole of my court waits to see how I will mark the victory.\n\nThe custom of the Druchii is the triumph: the army marches through the city in its finest armour, the captives are driven before it under the lash, and the Brides of Khaine take their pick of the strongest for the altars. A lord who denies his people their triumph is thought weak, and the weak do not live long in Naggaroth.

[triumph_foe.GetTitledName] is beaten. His soldiers lie in their thousands on the fields where they fell, and my necromancers walk among them already, whispering them back onto their feet.\n\nThe living vassals who served me expect some mark of the victory, and there is a certain pleasure in showing them what became of those who fought against me. Let them watch the defeated march again, in my colours.

[triumph_foe.GetTitledName] is beaten, yes-yes! Of course the victory was mine, mine alone, whatever lies the Warlords and Grey Seers are squeaking in the tunnels.\n\nThe clanrats want a great feast of the dead. The other Warlords want to claim the glory for themselves. Best to show them all, loudly and quickly, whose victory this was, before someone sharpens a knife.
Hold a grand triumph. Let the whole realm see it.
In twelve days the triumph is held. Every vassal of rank in my realm will think better of me.
A short parade will do.
No triumph. The victory speaks for itself.

The triumph is held. The army marches beneath garlands of flowers through streets packed so tight the people climb onto rooftops to see. First come the trumpeters and the captured banners of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName], then the wagons heaped with plunder, then the ranks of my soldiers singing, and at the last myself, crowned with laurel, my lords riding behind.\n\nAt the temple the priests bless the standards and the names of the fallen are read aloud. The feasting goes on for three days and nights.

The triumph is held. The black standards of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] are dragged through the streets and burned in the great square, and the priests sprinkle the ashes with holy water and salt. Flagellants march before the army, the temples ring every bell they have, and mothers hold up their children to see the soldiers who saved them from the end of all things.\n\nTonight the realm drinks. Tomorrow it begins to rebuild, and watches the north.

The triumph is held. A mound of skulls taken from the army of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] is raised before the host, and I climb it while the warriors beat their shields and roar the names of the Dark Gods. The prisoners are given to the fires. Sorcerers read omens in the smoke, and the omens are good.\n\nThe chieftains bend the knee one by one beneath the skull-heap. For now, none of them doubts who is the strongest.

The victory is honoured in the ancestor halls. The names of the fallen are carved into the stone beside those of their fathers, the Runelords hammer the oaths of the war into the anvil, and the kegs are broached until the halls ring with old songs about older grudges.\n\nEven the grimmest of the Elders raise their tankards. The grudge against [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] is struck through in the Book.

Da trophy-heap iz finished. It's got da heads of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName]'s best lads, all da banners and most of a cart, and I'm standin' right on top of it. Da boyz scream WAAAGH till dey fall over, da goblins steal everyfin' not nailed down, and somebody lets da squigs out.\n\nBest party ever. Two boyz died. Dat's a good party.

The triumph is held. The army marches through the city in black armour, crowds of Druchii hurl curses and filth at the captives of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] driven before it under the lash, and the Brides of Khaine dance in blood before the temple of the Lord of Murder. At sunset the hearts of the strongest captives are offered on the altars.\n\nThe nobility watch me from their balconies, measuring my strength. Today they find nothing to exploit.

The triumph is held. The soldiers of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] march through my capital once more, rank upon rank of grey dead with their wounds still open, wearing my colours. The living vassals watch in silence from the stands as the defeated bow to me, one after another.\n\nNo one cheers. It is not that kind of triumph. But no one will soon forget it.

The triumph is held. My clanrats drag the dead of [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] through the tunnels and feast until they are sick, the engineers set off warpstone fireworks that kill only a few dozen, and I squeak my great deeds from the top of a pile of loot until my throat is raw.\n\nThe other Warlords applaud. Some of them even mean it.
Glory to the victors!
And let [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] walk behind my horse in chains.
Then put [triumph_foe.GetTitledName] to death before the crowd.
My liege [From.GetTitledName] has held a great triumph for the victory over [triumph_foe.GetTitledName]. I rode in the procession among the lords of the realm, and it was a sight to remember.
Glory to my liege.

When the feasting is over, a band of veterans comes before my throne. They are the hardest of the men who fought in the war, scarred and sun-blackened, and their captain says that they have no wish to go home to their fields. They would rather serve me, and only me, for as long as I need them.
Rise. You are my guard now.
A guard of veterans (150 heavy infantry and 100 pikemen) joins your army at half the usual upkeep.
Pay them well and send them home.
The Wasteland Returns

Since the Emperor Dieter IV took the burghers' gold and sold them their freedom, the Wasteland and proud Marienburg have stood apart from the Empire, paying no taxes, sending no soldiers and laughing at the Emperor from behind their dykes and their ships.\n\nNo more. From Marienburg's harbour to the last fen of the Fauligmere, the lands of the Reik mouth answer to [Root.GetTitledName] again. The Empire has its sea gate back.
The Reik flows through one Empire again.
The Drakwald Cleansed

The Drakwald was a province of the Empire once, with an Elector of its own, until the beastmen came out of the trees and the plague came after them. Its last count died in the dark, his line ended, and his lands were given away to his neighbours or left to the herdstones.\n\nNow every village from Carroburg to the Laurelorn holds for [Root.GetTitledName]. The forest is still dark, and the beastmen are not gone. But the Drakwald is ours again.
Let the woodsmen go back to their axes.
Solland Avenged

In the year 1707 the Warboss Gorbad Ironclaw came over the Black Fire Pass with the greatest WAAAGH of the age. He slew the Elector Count Eldred of Solland, carried off the Solland Runefang, and left the province a wasteland of ashes. Solland never rose again, and Wissenland took what remained.\n\nNow Söll, Pfeildorf and the Sudenland all answer to [Root.GetTitledName]. In the ruined chapels the old folk light candles for Eldred.
Eldred is avenged.
The Empire of Sigmar Made Whole

Two and a half thousand years ago Sigmar Heldenhammer united the tribes of men and was crowned in Reikdorf. Since then the Empire has been torn by civil war, plague, Chaos, greenskins and its own greedy lords. Provinces have been lost, Electors murdered, and rival Emperors crowned in Talabheim and Middenheim.\n\nToday every province of the Empire, from the Middle Mountains to the Black Mountains and from the Wasteland to the Worlds Edge, answers to one Emperor: [Root.GetName]. The priests of Sigmar are calling it a miracle. The common people call it the return of the golden age.
One Empire, one Emperor, one god!
Eight Peaks Reclaimed

Karak Eight Peaks, Vala-Azrilungol, Queen of the Silver Depths, was the fairest hold of the Karaz Ankor. In the Time of Woes the skaven came up from below and the night goblins down from above, and King Lunn led the last of his people out into exile. For thousands of years the rats and goblins fought over the corpse of the hold.\n\nNow the Queen of the Silver Depths has a Dawi lord again. The great gates are rehung, the dead are laid to rest at last, and in every hold of the Karaz Ankor the grudge is struck through in the Book.
Vala-Azrilungol is ours. Strike the grudge from the Book!
Karak Varn Reclaimed

Karak Varn, the hold of the Black Water, was split by the earthquakes of the Time of Woes and the dark lake flooded its lower deeps. The skaven and the goblins poured in through the cracks, and the miners of the gromril seams were never seen again.\n\nNow Dawi lanterns burn in Karak Varn once more, and the old gromril seams are being cleared.
Back to the seams.
Mount Gunbad Reclaimed

Mount Gunbad, the richest of all the mines of the Karaz Ankor, fell to the night goblins in the Goblin Wars, and its tunnels became the den of a thousand tribes. Its gold built more than one goblin kingdom.\n\nNow the Dawi hold Gunbad again. The goblins have been smoked out of the deep galleries, and the hammers ring in the mines.
The gold of Gunbad comes home.
Karak Azgal Reclaimed

Karak Azgal was once Karak Izril, the Jewelled Hold, until Graug the Terrible came and coiled himself on its treasure. For centuries since, its halls have been a warren of goblins, skaven and worse, and a magnet for every treasure-hunter and fool in the Old World.\n\nNow the Dawi have their hold back, and they mean to give it its proper name again.
Karak Izril shines again.
Karak Ungor Reclaimed

Karak Ungor, the northernmost of the great holds, fell to the night goblins of the Red Eye in the Time of Woes. For millennia the goblins have squatted in its halls, and the Dawi have written its name in red in the Book of Grudges.\n\nNow the Red Eye has been put out. Karak Ungor is a Dawi hold again.
Another grudge settled.
The Karaz Ankor Made Whole

In the golden age of the Dawi, the Karaz Ankor ran the length of the Worlds Edge Mountains, from Karak Ungor in the north to Karak Azul in the south, linked by the Ungdrin Ankor. Earthquakes, skaven, goblins and the long war with the elves broke it into scattered holds, and every Dawi child is raised on the names of the holds that were lost.\n\nToday every hold of the Everpeak's realm is in Dawi hands again. The ancestors are watching, and for once they have nothing to complain about.
Grungni, Valaya, Grimnir: behold your children.
Nehekhara Restored

Before Nagash, before the Great Ritual, the Land of the Dead was Nehekhara, the fairest of the realms of men, ruled from Khemri by the Priest Kings. Then the Great Betrayer killed it all, and the kings woke in their tombs to find their land a desert of ruins and their cities fighting one another.\n\nNow, from Zandri to Lahmia and from Numas to Mahrak, every city of Nehekhara bows to the heir of the Priest Kings: [Root.GetTitledName]. The legions of the dead stand in the deserts as they stood in the age of glory, and the old gods are given their due again.
The Land of the Dead is one realm again.
With the death of [From.GetBestName], you are no longer [From.GetHerHis] tributary.
Free at last.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

Our realms have been on good terms for some time, and the world grows darker every year. Let us swear not to raise arms against each other for five years, so that each of us may face our true enemies without looking over our shoulder.

[From.GetTitledName]
Agreed. Five years of peace between us.
I will make no such promise.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I accept your offer. For five years, no army of mine will march against you. Let our enemies take note.

[From.GetTitledName]
Excellent.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I must refuse your offer. I will not bind my hands with promises at this time.

[From.GetTitledName]
How unfortunate.

Word of the revolt has spread through the realm, and the discontented flock to your banner: landless knights, broken men, hungry peasants and every lord with a grudge against [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Your host swells by the day.
Excellent!
Your scouts bring grim news. Men are flocking to the banner of the rebel [From.GetTitledName] from every corner of the realm, and the rebel host grows by the day.
Traitors, all of them.

The rebellion has dragged on for months, and the realm is tired of it. Loyal men who have watched the rebels burn their fields now come to your banner in their hundreds, eager to see the traitors hang.
Bad news from the enemy camp: loyalists are flocking to the banner of [From.GetTitledName], and the host raised against us grows stronger.
They will not save [From.GetHerHim].

The treasury is empty and the creditors are at the gates. Your steward suggests a quiet word with one of your vassals: a lord who owes you everything can surely spare a little gold for [Root.GetHerHis] liege.
Ask a rich vassal for 250 gold.
Ask a vassal for 50 gold.
Ask a vassal for 10 gold.
A rich vassal will be asked for 250 gold.\n
A vassal will be asked for 50 gold.\n
A vassal will be asked for 10 gold.\n
A letter from [From.GetTitledFirstName]: our liege's treasury is empty, and [From.GetSheHe] asks us, as a loyal vassal, to help fill it.
Pay, but [From.GetSheHe] will owe us for this.
You pay 250 gold, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] owes you a favour.\n
Pay what our liege asks.
Refuse. Let [From.GetHerHim] pay [From.GetHerHis] own debts.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has refused to send a single coin. The whole court knows of it by now.
Ungrateful wretch.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent the gold you asked for, with a letter full of loyal sentiments.
Splendid.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent the gold you asked for. The letter that came with it reminds you, very politely, that [From.GetSheHe] will expect something in return one day.
You receive 250 gold, and owe [From.GetTitledFirstName] a favour.\n
My coffers are empty, but the temples of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] are rich! Perhaps I should seize temple lands to pay my debts.
Seize the lands of those idle [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s!
The times are harsh. The cult will share the cost!
Find a compromise with the priests.
Never! I would never betray [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]!
The priests will not sit silent while temple lands are seized.\n
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] looks down upon weak souls such as [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Never in the history of the cult has a ruler sunk so low as to rob its temples!
[From.GetSheHeCap] is cursed in the eyes of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]!
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] can also be merciful.
[This.GetTitledFirstName] will be cast out of the cult of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] when the [Root.RelHead.GetRulerTitle] hears of this.\n
An emissary from the [Root.RelHead.GetRulerTitle] has come to our court to announce that we are anathema to the faithful of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]. We have been cast out!
Curse them all!

Everyone knows that [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] is drowning in debt. A generous offer of gold might persuade [Root.Liege.GetHerHim] to part with [event_target:title_for_sale.GetFullBaseName], to which we have a fair claim.
Offer 300 gold, and a favour owed.
Offer 200 gold.
Let it be.
Your liege may accept the offer.\n
[From.GetTitledFirstName] offers 200 gold for [event_target:title_for_sale.GetFullBaseName]. Your creditors would be glad of it.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] offers 300 gold for [event_target:title_for_sale.GetFullBaseName], and promises to remember your generosity.
Sell it.
It is not for sale.
The mercenaries you could not pay have taken their wages from the countryside instead. They are burning and looting their way through your lands.
Curse those sell-swords!
Unpaid and disgusted, the mercenaries in your service have packed up and left.
Good riddance.
The mercenaries you could not pay have sold their swords to the enemy!
Treacherous dogs!
The enemy could not pay their mercenaries, and the company has come over to our side.
Their gold is as good as anyone's.
The holy order fighting in your service has had enough and marched home.
So much for their oaths.

In honour of the Empire's victory, it would be fitting to hold a triumph in Altdorf for the brave soldiers who fought in the campaign. Such a celebration will be costly, but the people expect nothing less.
Yes, a glorious triumph will be held.
A brief parade through the streets will be enough.
No, we have no time for such nonsense.
A triumph is held in Altdorf.

A mighty triumph is held in Altdorf to celebrate the brave generals and soldiers who defeated the enemies of the Empire. The people cheer as the state troops march past the Temple of Sigmar, followed by wagons heavy with the spoils of war and cages holding captives from the campaign.
Sigmar's Empire stands strong.

The [From.GetTitle] has commanded that a triumph be held in Altdorf to celebrate the brave soldiers behind the Empire's victory. The people cheer as the state troops march past the Temple of Sigmar, followed by wagons heavy with the spoils of war and cages holding captives from the campaign.
An impressive display.

My coffers are empty, and I have already borrowed from my friends. The banking houses of Marienburg lend to any lord who can sign his name, and their factors are already waiting in the antechamber with ledgers under their arms...
My coffers are empty. The lending-clans of the Karaz Ankor will advance gold to any Dawi of good name, but they will want it back, every coin of it, and they never forget a debt.
My coffers are empty. The merchant houses of Araby, who trade from Al-Haikk to the far Ivory Road, will lend against my name, for a share of the profit.
They will make me such a deal!
I have no choice.
I will not be in anyone's debt!
Take a five-year loan of 200 gold at 25% interest
Take a five-year loan of 200 gold at 50% interest
The moneylenders inform me that my loan is due...
250 gold it is.
250 gold? Ask for more time.
Next year, it will be 300
The moneylenders are here, reminding me of that loan I took...
A grim Dawi reckoner stands before me with a ledger as thick as a door, reminding me of the loan I took. Every year it goes unpaid is written down in it, and my name with it.
300 gold? Very well.
I don't have the 300. Come back later.
Cut off their hands and throw them out!
Drakwald Restored

For nine hundred years Drakwald was a name on old maps and a curse in the mouths of woodsmen. Count Vilner fell around 1110 IC, no Elector was ever chosen in his place, and the beasts of the forest burned what the Goblins left. By 1414 Middenland and Nordland had shared out the bones, Nordland taking the lion's share. Now the duchies answer to one crown again, the Runefang of Drakwald comes home from the Emperor's vaults, and the old province of the Thuringians stands once more against the herds of the deep wood.
Count Vilner's line is gone. His charge is mine.

News from the north of the Empire: [From.GetTitledName] has raised Drakwald from its grave. The duchies that Middenland and Nordland shared out between them in 1414 now answer to a Drakwalder crown again, and the province's Runefang has come home. The Electors who lost the lands are not pleased.
Forgotten, but not lost.
Solland Restored

In 1707 IC the Waaagh of Gorbad Ironclaw burned Solland from the Black Mountains to the Reik. At Solland's Crown the Warboss tore the crown from the head of Elector Count Eldred and set it on his own, and Wissenland swallowed what was left. For three hundred years the sons of Solland kept the sun on their crests and the name Sudenland on their lips. Now Pfeildorf flies the sun banner again, the Sollanders have their crown back, and the province stands once more.
Let the greenskins come again. Solland will be waiting.

News from the south of the Empire: [From.GetTitledName] has raised Solland again. The lands Wissenland took after Gorbad's Waaagh in 1707 now answer to a Sollander crown, and the sun banner flies over Pfeildorf. Wissenland's Elector is not pleased.
Crushed, but never defeated.
My clerks and bailiffs have not been paid in months. In §Y[Root.GetName]§! the courts sit empty, the tithes go unrecorded, and every petty lordling settles his quarrels with the sword.
I will pay them when I can.

With the watch unpaid, the streets of §Y[Root.GetName]§! belong to the cutpurses. A guild of thieves now takes its cut from every market stall and counting house. Its masters have sent word that a share could find its way to me, if my eyes were to turn elsewhere.
Curse them. I will hang them all when the coffers are full.
Gold is gold. Let them have their streets.

The toll keepers of §Y[Root.GetName]§! have gone unpaid, and smugglers now run the rivers and the coast in the dark. Untaxed goods, plague-ridden cargo and worse pass through my lands. The smugglers would gladly share their takings with a ruler who does not ask what is in the crates.
I will deal with them later.
Let them sail, and pay me for the privilege.
My roadwardens have gone unpaid and have left their posts. Robber bands now hold the roads of §Y[Root.GetName]§!, and no carter, pilgrim or recruiting sergeant dares the highway without an escort.
The roads were never safe anyway.
Robber bands may take to the roads of one of your provinces.
My treasury is out of the red, and the clerks and bailiffs of §Y[Root.GetName]§! have been paid at last. The courts sit again, and the lordlings put up their swords.
Order is restored.
